newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bankers Trust Australia sees growth in processing.
newsitem.headline: Bankers Trust Australia sees growth in processing.

text.p: Bankers Trust Australia Ltd said on Thursday it saw a new growth business opportunity in offering its processing services to other fund managers.
Bankers Trust managing director Rob Ferguson told a business luncheon in Adelaide BT's large size and advanced systems meant its processing operations was highly efficient.
"We have come to the conclusion that if we can do that for ourselves, we should be doing it for others as well," he said.
"In other words, we will also be offering these processing services to other fund managers, along with corporates and (superannuation) funds which use our custody services," he said.
BT Australia is a unit of Bankers Trust New York Corp .
"We are going to become a world class operator in the processing business and we mean to win a big market share," he said.
Ferguson later told Reuters that BT, which will launch the new strategy from its new, dedicated processing facility in Adelaide, did not yet have any specific volume targets.
"We can just smell the opportunity, but we have not worried too much about quantifying it (yet)," he said, but added that potential customers had already demonstrated interest.
He said he expected to sign up customers in the next six months but he "would not be thinking about it being significant in a profit sense for three, four, five years time."

Ferguson said BT would target other fund managers, mainly in Australia but also potentially in New Zealand, which may have core competence in funds management but were not so well equipped to run complicated and expensive processing systems.
While some competition was likely, particularly from offshore, BT believed it had a competitive advantage in Australia, through its scale and local applications, he said.
"We have the systems already so we have a lead time on those competitors, we are getting to it and we are going to get a big market share in the meantime," he said.
The new Adelaide centre, which will run BT's securities and investor services businesses, will begin operations with about 130 staff, rising eventually to 540, he said.
